Sam (CS): Hi all — Acme (Marco) reported a burst of 429s during SDK init when their CI spins up ~150 workers. Happens right at the first warmup wave. Can someone help triage? :wave:
Priya (Eng): Thanks Sam. Marco, can you paste the client-side headers and the server X-Rate-Limit headers if you have them? Also which SDK version?
Marco (Customer): Using js-sdk v2.1.0 in our runner. We saw this in the logs:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-limit: 60
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 45
```
We hit it within 30s of starting.
Sam (CS): They spawn 150 parallel init requests in CI warmup job.
Olivia (SRE): That pattern looks like a classic preflight fanout. If each worker does a preflight handshake concurrently you slam the token/conn budget.
Priya (Eng): Agree. Two immediate levers: 1) client-side pacing/jitter on SDK init, 2) enable HTTP keepalive + connection reuse so handshakes amortize. Can you show how you call init?
Marco (Customer): We do naive parallel map on replicas: `workers.map(w => sdk.init({key: ENV.KEY}))` — all at once.
Priya (Eng): Ok. Quick patch: add a small randomized delay before init and limit concurrent inits. Example pseudocode:
```
await pMap(workers, async w => {
  await sleep(rand(100, 800)) // jitter
  await sdk.init({key})
}, {concurrency: 6})
```
That should keep preflight fanout under the 60rpm-ish token window.
Sam (CS): Also try setting keepalive on Node: `agent: new https.Agent({keepAlive: true, maxSockets: 50})` — reduces connection churn.
Olivia (SRE): From infra side we can temporarily bump their rate bucket for onboarding tests and monitor. But long-term client pacing is safer.
onboard-bot: Note: opened CS ticket #CS-1029 and temporary rate bump requested for org-acme.
Marco (Customer): Implemented the jitter + concurrency:6 and enabled keepalive. Re-ran CI — no 429s during the warmup wave now. Thanks! :tada:
Priya (Eng): Nice. We'll add a small cookbook snippet to onboarding docs: "stagger SDK init and reuse connections for CI warmups". Sam — can you capture this as part of the enablement playbook and flag renewal risk as mitigated?
Sam (CS): Will do. Adding the steps and the resolved note to the account health doc for Acme.
Olivia (SRE): Leaving a monitoring alert tweak: increase alarm window to 1m to reduce noisy flaps during rolling warmups.
Marco (Customer): Confirmed all good on our side. Appreciate the fast help.
Sam (CS): Great, closing loop. If they need a longer ramp or dedicated quota during big scale tests we can coordinate with sales for a temporary Dedicated trial."
